findings.title: Concurrent mutations can overwrite persisted collaboration state
findings.why_it_matters: All mutation methods change shared document maps before awaiting refreshAndSave, but the engine has no per-process serialization. Two overlapping tool calls can build different XML snapshots and race on the same BPMN path; the later write to finish can omit a successful participant, owner process, or flow mutation, so reopening loses collaboration state even though both calls returned successfully.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize mutations and saves per process (or stage an immutable candidate and commit it only after persistence), then add a concurrent create/connect test that reopens the file and asserts every mutation is present.
evidence: src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:162-163 and :223-224 mutate context.elements/context.connections and immediately await refreshAndSave without a lock or queue.
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:394-404 serializes and writes the shared process filename for every operation; overlapping calls have no ordering or compare-and-swap check.
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:203-204 builds the snapshot and reaches asynchronous bpmn-moddle XML generation at :380, leaving an interleaving window before either save completes.

findings.title: Failed saves leave the in-memory ownership model committed
findings.why_it_matters: Participant creation adds a process root and mutation methods update shared maps/objects before serializer and filesystem errors are returned. If mkdir, serialization, or writeFile fails, the caller receives an error but the live context retains the new process/element/flow; subsequent operations can serialize an orphan process or other state that was never durably committed, while a restart reopens the prior file.
findings.suggested_fix: Stage document changes on a clone, persist the candidate atomically, and publish the candidate to the live process only after the write succeeds; otherwise restore all maps, process roots, DI, and context.xml on failure.
evidence: src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:103-109 inserts a generated participant process root before the element is added and before refreshAndSave can fail.
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:162-164, :223-225, :250-258, and :300-315 all publish mutations before the awaited persistence boundary.
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:400-404 propagates filesystem errors after attempting to write the live context, with no rollback or temporary-file/rename transaction.

residual_risks: The direct fs.writeFile save path is non-atomic and can leave a truncated BPMN file on interruption or storage failure; this behavior predates the selected collaboration ownership changes and should be tracked separately from bead mcp-bpmn-9sv.2.
testing_gaps: No focused test runs overlapping createElement/connect/updateElement calls and then reopens the saved collaboration to detect lost writes.
No focused test injects mkdir, serializer, or writeFile failure and verifies that the live ownership/process maps and persisted XML remain unchanged after the rejected mutation.
